title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): S is a scheme and M is a rank-4 Azumaya algebra over O_S, i.e. a Zariski/étale form of M_2(O_S); in the main case M = End_{O_S}(F) with F locally free of rank 2. The associated groups are G = M^* (a form of GL_2), SG (norm 1, a form of SL_2) and PG (a form of PGL_2). On the previous page, a section of M is called 'regular' if in no fibre it is a scalar (i.e. it lies in the centre nowhere). The page opens by finishing the previous corollary: two sections ρ, ρ' with ρ regular are locally conjugate iff ρ' is regular and they have the same det and Tr. This follows from the equivalence a)⇔d) of the earlier proposition.

Proposition. Write ε = 1+N, a section of M. Using the rank-2 identities det(1+N) = 1 + Tr N + det N and Tr(1+N) = 2 + Tr N (correct), the following are equivalent:
- a) det ε = 1, Tr ε = 2 and ε is regular.
- b) det N = Tr N = 0 and N is regular. By Cayley–Hamilton this gives N^2 = 0, and N vanishes in no fibre.
- c) (case M = End(F)) There is a line subbundle D ⊂ F with N(F) = D and N(D) = 0. Here D = Im N = Ker N is determined by N, and D determines N up to a unit, since N is a nowhere-vanishing section of the line bundle Hom(F/D, D).
- c') Locally there is a basis e_0, e_1 with N = [[0,1],[0,0]], i.e. ε = [[1,1],[0,1]].
- d) There is a Borel subgroup B ⊂ G such that ε is a section of the unipotent radical B_u that is nowhere equal to 1.
- d') The same with a Borel subgroup SB ⊂ SG and (SB)_u.

Moreover D, B and SB are determined by ε and determine N up to homothety. B is the stabiliser of D, and B_u ≅ Hom(F/D, D) is a line bundle, so ε corresponds to a nowhere-zero section of it.

Definitions. ε is '(strictly) unipotent' if det ε = 1 and Tr ε = 2. N is 'strictly nilpotent' if det N = Tr N = 0. They are 'regular unipotent' / 'regular nilpotent' if in addition they are regular.

Purpose. This is part of building, scheme-theoretically over an arbitrary base, the dictionary for forms of GL_2/SL_2/PGL_2: regular elements, conjugacy by numerical invariants, regular unipotents ↔ Borels. The next page continues with elementary projectors ↔ Killing pairs (B,T). It serves as groundwork for the 'équation des lacets' material (presumably SL_2/PSL_2-type structures attached to the Teichmüller/Lego tower), though this page is not explicitly connected to it.
errors: No substantive error. The proofs are routine.

Note on the word 'strictement': over a non-reduced base, nilpotent does not imply det N = Tr N = 0. For example N = η·1 with η^2 = 0 is nilpotent but has Tr N = 2η. Hence the qualifier 'strictly', which Grothendieck then lets drop in the regular case. It is a sound and careful distinction.

'D determines N up to homothety' should be read as: up to an invertible section of O_S, given that Hom(F/D, D) is trivialised by N. Globally N determines that line bundle as trivial, and D alone determines N only up to Γ(O_S^*).

ideas.what: Regular sections of a rank-4 Azumaya algebra / forms of GL_2 as nowhere-central sections; conjugacy determined by Tr and det for regular elements
ideas.modern_name: Regular elements in reductive group schemes; companion-matrix/cyclic-vector normal form over a base
ideas.where_published: SGA3 Exp. XIII–XIV (regular elements, Cartan subgroups) in general form

ideas.what: Regular unipotent sections correspond to (Borel subgroup, nowhere-trivial section of its unipotent radical); D = Im N = Ker N
ideas.modern_name: Regular unipotent elements lie in a unique Borel (Springer/Steinberg), here for rank-2 forms over a base
ideas.where_published: Borel subgroups over a base in SGA3 Exp. XXII; this specific statement unsure

ideas.what: Distinction strictly nilpotent (det = tr = 0) vs nilpotent over non-reduced bases
ideas.modern_name: Scheme-theoretic nilpotent cone defined by invariant polynomials (Kostant–Chevalley)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely standard linear algebra over a base for forms of GL_2/SL_2 (regular unipotents ↔ Borels), in the style of SGA3. Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The number '975' written above 'l'équivalence' in the first line appears to be a marginal page/reference number (likely a cross-reference), not part of the sentence.

In the Definition, the wording reads roughly 'on [dit] ~ appelle ... ε est (strictement) unipotent si on a det ε = 1, Tr ε = 2, que N est strictement nilpotent si det N = tr N = 0'. Here 'si' replaces a struck 'dit' before det N; the exact struck word is uncertain.
In c), the original phrase is '(Alors D est uniquement déterminé par ε i.e. par N, D détermine N mod homothétie)'. The 'D détermine...' part is an interlinear addition.
